% Grounding & evaluation -- findings and provenance (generated by src/reporting/export_latex.py)
% Analysis code: branch grounding-evaluation, commit ede31b8
% Benchmark: data/combined_benchmark_500.json, SHA-256 bb79a6dbe6cc6b5c...
% Two evaluation layers are reported separately: (i) Python IR execution + deterministic answer
% evaluator (src/evaluation/ir_executor.py, answer_evaluator.py) and (ii) Z3 SMT verification (Sam's verifier).

\paragraph{E1. Evidence grounding checker (validation).}
\begin{itemize}
\item Deterministic checker that ties every IR number to a table cell or text span (formats, signs, \%, stated scale).
\item On reference IR from 468 FinQA gold programs it returns PASS for 463/468; the rest are gold programs that
  write a filing fact as a constant. It detects 100\% of injected $\times$1000, sign and wrong-reference errors
  (Table~\ref{tab:grounding-validation}).
\item Limitation: a wrong year that is \emph{cited} correctly passes grounding by design; grounding is not answer correctness.
\item Provenance: \texttt{src/experiments/run\_grounding\_evaluation.py}; no model; FinQA cases of the 500-case benchmark; commit ede31b8.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{E2. GPT-4o-mini answers: Python evaluator vs Z3 verdict.}
\begin{itemize}
\item Lenient answer accuracy 72.3\% (349/483) on all scored cases and 58.7\% (44/75) on the 80 NOT\_APPLICABLE cases
  (Table~\ref{tab:answer-accuracy}).
\item A Z3 PASS does not imply a correct answer: 76.2\% (93/122) of PASS cases match gold vs 72.4\% (244/337) of NOT\_APPLICABLE cases
  (Z3 checks the stated arithmetic, not the financial question).
\item 30 of 484 FinQA gold answers disagree with their own reference program. Checked by hand against the
  evidence: in 11 the gold answer is wrong (e.g.\ F\_151 3829 vs 38290), in 13 the program is wrong but
  the answer right (e.g.\ F\_222), 5 are wrong on both sides and 1 is ambiguous
  (Table~\ref{tab:gold-audit}). Only the 6 without a reliable reference need excluding.
\item Provenance: model gpt-4o-mini (stored answers, \texttt{results/verification\_results.json});
  \texttt{src/experiments/run\_answer\_evaluation.py} (Python evaluator; Z3 verdicts from the original verifier); commit ede31b8.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{E3. Grounding of Stage~1~v2 equations (80 cases).}
\begin{itemize}
\item Of the equation inputs Stage~1~v2 extracted, 70.6\% (48/68) appear directly in the evidence; 4 are not found
  (Table~\ref{tab:stage1-grounding}).
\item 19 cases have all-PASS arithmetic and fully grounded inputs, but only 12 match gold: most of the rest
  have disputed gold answers, and F\_089 uses the wrong denominator -- an error neither grounding nor arithmetic checks catch.
\item Provenance: \texttt{src/experiments/run\_stage1\_grounding.py} on Chaewon's Stage~1~v2 results; no gold used for grounding; commit ede31b8.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{E4. Autoformalization pilot: 3-shot vs 8-shot (16 cases).}
\begin{itemize}
\item No grounding errors in either configuration: every IR input is found in the cited cell, sentence or evidence line.
\item Formalization accuracy (Python execution of the IR equations vs gold) is 12/16 (75\%) for 3-shot and
  13/16 (81\%) for 8-shot (10/11 (91\%) vs
  11/11 (100\%) excluding disputed gold); 8-shot fixes the F\_089 denominator (Table~\ref{tab:pilot}).
\item Most validator arithmetic mismatches are errors in the formalized GPT-4o-mini answer that the IR exposes: the
  equations are right but the claimed value is copied: F\_015 equations give \pounds 933.39 (= gold) vs the claimed \pounds 916.35,
  F\_011 \$9{,}458.51 (= gold) vs \$9{,}469.51.
\item Limitations: 16 cases, one model, one sample per configuration (API defaults, no seed); the difference is one case.
\item Provenance: runner \texttt{experiments/autoformalization/autoformalize.py} (branch chaewon/finqa-autoformalization;
  14 cases on 7522e82; F\_011 and F\_015 rerun on dc8ce86 after the evidence fix; prepared inputs of the 14 identical on both);
  model gpt-6.2-sol (Responses API, strict JSON schema, API defaults); scoring \texttt{src/experiments/run\_ir\_grounding.py}
  (Python IR execution, not Z3); OpenAI usage for the pilot including both reruns: 36 requests, 115,336 tokens, \$0.56 (project dashboard, November).
\end{itemize}
